questions.q: Which shape does ComfyUI use for an IMAGE tensor?
options: [H, W, C] with no batch axis
questions.why: The ComfyUI datatype documentation gives [B, H, W, C], and LoadImage builds exactly that. The LATENT samples use [B, C, H/8, W/8], which is why the VAE nodes call movedim.

questions.q: On an IMAGE tensor, why is reshape(B, C, H, W) not the same as movedim(-1, 1)?
options: reshape always makes a copy and movedim never does
reshape keeps the memory order and only relabels the axes, so the shape is right but the pixels are mixed
movedim changes the values and reshape does not
questions.answer: reshape keeps the memory order and only relabels the axes, so the shape is right but the pixels are mixed
questions.why: In the lab, channel 0 of an all-red image is 100% red after movedim and 33.3% red after reshape, and Conv2d accepts both without an error.

questions.q: What does VAEEncode do with a 515 by 333 image?
questions.why: vae_encode_crop_pixels cuts each side down to a multiple of 8, taking the extra pixels from both ends. The lab prints 515x333 -> 512x328 and a latent of [1, 4, 41, 64].

questions.q: After the decoder, ComfyUI computes (x + 1) / 2 and then clamps. What does the clamp do for a decoder output of -1.2?
options: It maps it to 0.0 after (x + 1) / 2 gave -0.1
questions.answer: It maps it to 0.0 after (x + 1) / 2 gave -0.1
questions.why: process_output adds 1, divides by 2 and clamps to 0..1. The lab row shows -1.20 -> -0.10 -> 0.00.

questions.q: How many bytes does a float32 IMAGE batch of 4 images at 1024 by 1024 occupy?
questions.why: 4 x 1024 x 1024 x 3 values x 4 bytes = 50,331,648 bytes, which is 48 MiB. The lab prints it, and the same batch as uint8 would be 12 MiB.

questions.q: The lab adds 0.1 to the 256 eight-bit levels in float32, subtracts it again, and saves the way SaveImage does. How many levels come back unchanged?
options: All 256 when the cast truncates, and fewer when it rounds
237 when the cast truncates and all 256 when it rounds
All 256 in both cases because float32 is exact
questions.answer: 237 when the cast truncates and all 256 when it rounds
questions.why: Some results land a hair below a whole number, and a truncating cast takes them down one level. SaveImage uses astype(np.uint8), which truncates; the lab prints 237 for truncation and 256 for rounding.
